title: DMC3 HD startup path: the only wholly sound route through the image

records.title: 370 functions, seventeen deep, and every platform subsystem brought up inside them
records.summary: Direct calls and tail jumps from the entry point reach 370 of the image's 7,389 functions, and that closure assumes nothing about dispatch, which makes it the only route through the image that is sound end to end. It runs seventeen steps deep and bulges between five and eight, where 290 of the 370 functions and 116 kilobytes of code sit. Inside it the programme calls 97 symbols across 18 modules, and that set is the whole platform: Direct3D and DXGI, DirectInput, XInput, FMOD, Steam, USER32, KERNEL32 and the C runtime. The entry stub reaches the runtime's own startup by a tail jump rather than a call, so a closure following calls alone stops at two functions instead of 370 — which is why the depth counts transfers.

locations.note: RVA 0x34615C, eighteen bytes, reaching the runtime's startup by a tail jump.

records.title: Not one of the image's 396 classes is constructed on the sound path
records.summary: Of the 370 functions the startup path reaches, zero are identified as constructors, and only 30 contain a dispatch at all, over 68 sites. So the boundary is sharp: the sound path brings the platform up and then hands off, and everything the engine builds is built on the other side of a virtual call. This is the same fact that made the rapid-type tightening of the reachability bound collapse to four vtables, stated at its source rather than as a symptom. It also sets what a port must have standing before any object exists: 97 imported symbols and the 67 fixed addresses the path operates on.

records.title: Each platform subsystem is brought up by one identifiable function
records.summary: Reading what each function on the path imports names it without naming it: the compiler's import table is the evidence, not a guess. RVA 0x42890, 2,024 bytes and the sole caller of either symbol, calls CreateDXGIFactory and D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain and carries six dispatch sites, which are the calls on the interfaces it creates. RVA 0x47B40, 1,217 bytes and again a sole caller, calls RegisterClassExW, CreateWindowExW, ShowWindow, UpdateWindow, GetSystemMetrics, MonitorFromWindow, GetMonitorInfoW and SetWindowsHookExW together with DirectInput8Create: window creation and input device creation in one function. RVA 0x3A9E0 calls SteamInternal_ContextInit beside OutputDebugStringW, and RVA 0x41BC0 calls XInputGetState guarded by GetFocus. Each is a single point a port has to replace.

locations.note: RVA 0x42890, the only function in the image calling either D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain or CreateDXGIFactory.
RVA 0x47B40, the only caller of DirectInput8Create, with the full Win32 window-class and window creation sequence beside it.

records.title: A 157-byte function read end to end from its imports and its compare chain
records.summary: RVA 0x48970 is 157 bytes with no dispatch sites and one caller. It calls PeekMessageW, then on a message TranslateMessage and DispatchMessageW, which is the whole of its import set beside one more. Its compare chain is readable: the retrieved message number is compared against 0x12 and, when it is at or below, tested against the bit mask 0x50004, which selects exactly the values 2, 16 and 18. On those three it takes a different exit, and that exit calls through the thunk at RVA 0x3454C8, which jumps to the import-address-table slot at 0x34F700 that the import directory names fmod64.dll!FMOD_System_UnlockDSP, and then returns zero rather than one. So the audio call is on the way out, not once a frame. The three message numbers are named WM_DESTROY, WM_CLOSE and WM_QUIT by the Win32 headers; that naming is public interface knowledge rather than anything read from this file, and the values are what the file gives.

locations.note: RVA 0x48970: PeekMessageW at 0x48998, the mask 0x50004 tested at 0x489B0, the FMOD thunk called at 0x489CA.

records.title: The sound path extends by exactly zero functions through dispatch
records.summary: The dispatches the startup path makes were described as the handoff; reading all of them shows the handoff is total. Of the 99 sites, 88 have nothing known about the receiver, 10 read it through one of the argument registers and one through an address the code took. Not one resolves to a class and a target, so the number of functions the sound closure gains by following a determined dispatch is zero. The reason is structural rather than a shortfall of the analysis: resolving a dispatch needs the enclosing function to be one the compiler bound into a vtable, and of the 370 functions on the path exactly none is. The platform is brought up by free functions, and the first virtual call is the last thing the file lets anyone follow.

records.title: Correction: 99 dispatch sites on the startup path, not 68
records.summary: The startup path was published as carrying 68 dispatch sites. That figure came from a narrower list than the image-wide census of 11,434 printed beside it: it counts only the call-position dispatches and omits the tail-position ones, which are the same dispatch by another instruction and which the census does count. Counting from the same list gives 99, of which 31 are in tail position. The figure of 30 functions containing a dispatch is unaffected, and so is everything the path was said to contain; only the site count moves.
